A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 44-page versions of the same DAISI work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original Gaussian-mixture, Lorenz ’63, SQG, and SEVIR experiments, including numerical comparisons and ablations in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 reports original experimental results on the same systems, including filtering accuracy, ensemble calibration, and component and hyperparameter ablations.

M1.justification: The forecast, backward inverse-sampling, and forward guided-sampling procedure is unchanged. DAISI-ML renames the learned-forecast variant already evaluated in v2 Table 14. The consistent exchange of alpha and beta notation does not change the interpolant or training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use the Gaussian-mixture example, Lorenz ’63, SQG at both resolutions, and SEVIR. Noisy, sparse, multimodal, saturating, longer-interval, and moving-observation scenarios were already present in v2. The expanded SQG description documents retained coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain BPF, LETKF, FlowDAS, EnSF, and SDA filtering and smoothing in their corresponding experiments. The additional columns in v4 Table 3 reproduce comparisons already reported in v2 Tables 12 and 14.

E3.justification: The stated metric specification changes: v2 Eq. (127) averages per-variable SSR ratios, whereas v4 Eq. (97) uses spread divided by pooled RMSE. The rewritten CRPS expression also omits the explicit grid normalization. These revisions do not establish recalculation of the retained scores; other experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The inversion, SDEdit, learned-forecast, hyperparameter, assimilation-interval, and non-stationary-observation analyses are retained. Their relocation and the additional visualization of existing observation operators do not introduce new ablations or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same reporting practices: means and standard deviations across ten experiments or trajectories, Lorenz ’63 credible intervals, and the single-run high-resolution evaluation. No additional repetitions, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, v4 Table 3’s DAISI-ML SQG CRPS values of 1.34, 1.72, 1.78, and 1.53 reproduce v2 Table 14. Its SEVIR entry repeats the existing DAISI result, which already used the learned forecaster.

T1.justification: v4 adds the explicit SQG governing equation, Eq. (113), and revises metric definitions, particularly SSR aggregation. The entropy-contraction proposition, assumptions, and proof are retained in Appendix E. The alpha/beta exchange is equivalent notation, not new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: stationary generative priors combined with forecast inversion, compatibility with numerical and learned forecasters, modular guidance, and accurate filtering under challenging observations.

C2.justification: v4 expands limitations concerning guidance bias and simplified operational conditions, adds correction and distillation directions, and removes the earlier iterative-noising compatibility caveat. Section 4.2 newly describes tuning as minimal, although Appendix C.4.6 retains the finding that tmin substantially affects performance.

D1.justification: v4 adds DAISI code-access information, identifies the Berzelius computing resource, and documents the SQG equation and zero Ekman-damping setting. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish a changed simulator. Existing architecture, training, and hyperparameter details remain.

R1.justification: Targeted references are added for distillation, stochastic flow maps, and modern weather forecasting and assimilation, including Boffi, Potaptchik, and Huang and colleagues. The decoupled-noise-annealing citation is removed. Savary’s updated title and venue correspond to the previously discussed work; DAISI’s main positioning remains.

P1.justification: Focused restructuring integrates the separate SDA discussion into Section 4.2, moves entropy dissipation to the final appendix, and adds dedicated limitations, acknowledgements, and impact sections. SQG explanations, metric notation, and author information are edited, while most prose remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 becomes a full-width comparison incorporating retained appendix results. Figure 5 adds an observation-operator visualization, and Figure 7 reformats the existing Sparse example for the main text. Appendix figures are regrouped; the original plots remain available.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves transparency through consolidated comparisons, code-access information, fuller SQG documentation, and clearer limitations. The empirical foundation remains unchanged. Less explicit metric aggregation and the stronger minimal-tuning interpretation temper these gains, but the documentation and presentation improvements provide a limited net benefit.
